items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-19
items.q: The interviewee confirms Charlie DeVore plays in the Hall Brothers band ('Right.') but does not describe a personal relationship, collaboration, or mentorship with DeVore himself.

ctx.x: He apparently was very conscious of the racial question.

Well, that's what I kept hearing all the time. But it never seemed to manifest itself in actual relationships. As a matter of fact, I considered that there was less of that in Charlie's personality than in most of the musicians that I know. He was perfectly prepared to take any individual on his face value, regardless of his color. And I don't think that he felt oppressed by being black. Certainly no more than other musicians have. Like, I know black musicians who, for instance, won't eat fried chicken or…
Are there any musicians that do not relate so much to the New Orleans style that you are particularly impressed by or with? Yeah, of course.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Charlie DeVore is a particular interest because he plays in the Hall Brothers Band in Mendota. [INTERVIEWEE] Right.

ctx.x: But I might mention that Johnny Wiggs was the teacher of Charlie DeVore.
